Jace Yarbrough

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 32, Dallas County, Texas · Open seat

Attorney and businessman; U.S. Air Force veteran

Jace Yarbrough is a Republican attorney and U.S. Air Force veteran running for the open U.S. House seat in Texas' 32nd Congressional District. He led the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 49.0% of the vote. The May 26 runoff was canceled after runner-up Ryan Binkley withdrew, and Yarbrough advanced to face Democrat Dan Barrios on November 3, 2026.

Where Yarbrough stands

Immigration and border
Supports President Trump's mass deportation efforts and more resources for ICE and DHS. Opposes all amnesty proposals and says legal immigration should not be used to drive down American wages.
Cost of living and economy
Says he will work to lower energy and grocery costs, protect Social Security and Medicare, and promote policies that expand access to home ownership.
Congressional ethics
Supports banning insider trading by members of Congress.
Gun policy
Supports national concealed-carry reciprocity and repeal of the National Firearms Act.
Health care
Opposes vaccine mandates and says he defended first responders who were fired over them. Says reducing food additives and chemicals would help lower health care costs.
Trade and China
Supports holding China accountable for unfair trade practices, promoting U.S. manufacturing and blue-collar jobs, and winning the AI race.
Energy
Supports expanding American energy production and opposes Green New Deal policies, which he says he challenged in court as a lawyer.
Foreign policy and veterans
Supports an America First foreign policy in which allies pay their fair share, and says this would allow better care for veterans.
Abortion
Describes himself as "100% pro-life" and says he opposed abortion providers in court over marketing abortions to minors.

Background

  • Republican nominee for U.S. House, Texas District 32 (2026); won the March 3, 2026 primary with 49.0%
  • Attorney (constitutional litigation, according to his campaign) and businessman
  • U.S. Air Force veteran (officer)
  • B.A., University of Texas at Austin
  • J.D., Stanford Law School, 2018
  • Co-founder, with his wife, of a classical Christian academy (per his campaign)
